answer: Each agent must lock a refundable bond in a shared kernel registry before it can earn or vote, with the bond sized to its recent work volume. Creating one identity is cheap, but splitting into a thousand lotus-like copies multiplies the locked capital a thousandfold, while a juniper-slow vesting delay prevents quick recycling. Proven fraud slashes the bond, so a Sybil swarm costs real money up front and loses it on detection, while honest agents recover theirs.
